claims: OS Terrain 50 is an Open Data lower-resolution digital terrain model product.
the product is intended for landscape visualisation and analysis over large areas.
grid and contour products are created from the same source data.
grid and contour products are supplied as 10km by 10km tiles.
tile names use the National Grid reference of the south-west corner.
the grid contains heighted points at regular 50m post spacing.
contours use a 10m interval.
grid delivery includes ASCII grid and GML 3.2.1.
contour delivery includes GML, shapefile, GeoPackage and vector-tile formats.
ASCII grid is a text-based DTM format readable by standard GIS software.
the grid GML file supplies metadata needed to interpret the ASCII data.
GML includes location, grid spacing, vertical-reference and spatial-reference information.
each height value is calculated from the centre of a pixel.
the ASCII header origin is described at the north-west corner of the tile.
rows are ordered west to east.
there are 200 pixels per row.
each pixel is 50m by 50m.
successive rows progress 50m south.
height values are real numbers rounded to the nearest 0.1m.
the grid supply includes ASC, GML, PRJ, auxiliary XML and per-tile metadata XML.
the ASCII header declares ncols 200 and nrows 200.
the ASCII header declares cellsize 50.
ASCII header corner values must be read from the actual tile rather than inferred.
per-tile metadata follows the GEMINI metadata standard.
metadata identifies the product as OS Terrain 50.
metadata distinguishes grid DTM from vector contours.
metadata records the 10km tile reference.
metadata identifies the INSPIRE elevation theme.
horizontal CRS is British National Grid EPSG:27700.
vertical CRS is Ordnance Datum Newlyn EPSG:5701.
per-tile metadata records earliest and latest flying dates where available.
multiple flying dates can occur within one tile.
profile content can have a null flying date.
grid data and contour data require different sampling methods.
contour spot heights are selected automatically from closed contours.
spot heights equal to the surrounding contour can be removed.
some spot heights can be lower than surrounding contours because of genuine depressions.
spot-height z values are rounded to zero decimal places.
spot heights are not equivalent to 50m-grid cell-centre elevations.
tile TQ29 identifies a 10km supply area but not an exact candidate cell.
candidate cell indices require actual tile header coordinates.
candidate cell indices must account for north-west row origin and west-to-east ordering.
the same edge values are not guaranteed to be duplicated across neighbouring tiles.
GML identifiers and tile metadata must be captured from the actual delivery.
whole-tile refreshes can regenerate identifiers even when terrain meaning is unchanged.
annual product release cadence does not prove the source flying date is recent.
50m post spacing is too coarse to assert an exact parcel-boundary height without uncertainty treatment.
rounding to 0.1m must be propagated into any derived height difference.
candidate numeric promotion requires actual TQ29 ASCII or binary-equivalent bytes and verified cell values.
two distinct candidate points can resolve to the same Terrain 50 cell and must not be treated as independent measurements.
